title: Senior Manager, Quality SME (HV/Substation)
text:
**Description**
Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Department: EHSQ / Quality
 
 
Location: Houston, TX
 
 
Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality
 
 
Direct Reports: None
 
 
FLSA Status: Exempt
 
 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time
 
 
Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote
 
 
Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.
 
 
The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.
 
 
**Summary**
The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on high-voltage, substation, and transmission construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on HV and substation scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers collector substations, switchyards and points of interconnection, and generation tie-lines (gen-tie); medium-voltage collection systems remain within the scope of Electrical Quality.
 
 
The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active HV, substation, or gen-tie construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of HV and substation Quality across the portfolio.
 
 
Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors, combined with the judgment to translate engineering, utility, manufacturer, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and Transmission & Distribution (T&D) teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, relay and protection settings, and functional commissioning remain with Engineering and Commissioning; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.
 
 
This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.
 
 
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time."
 
 
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Serve as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on HV, substation, switchyard, point of interconnection, and gen-tie construction, supporting the Senior Director of Quality and the Regional Quality Managers.
* Develop, own, and maintain company-standard ITP templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, SWIs, and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) content for HV and substation scopes, ensuring they reflect current engineering standards, manufacturer requirements, utility requirements, and lessons learned.
* Build and maintain HV and substation inspection templates and workflows in Procore, in coordination with Quality Systems, so that discipline inspections are performed and recorded consistently across all projects.
* Integrate with the assigned Regional Quality Manager on each project containing HV, substation, or gen-tie scope, from pre-mobilization planning through turnover, confirming discipline requirements are incorporated into the Site-Specific Quality Management Plan (SSQMP), ITPs, inspection staffing plan, and inspection schedule.
* Support the Preconstruction Quality SME by tailoring discipline ITPs and checklists for project kickoff packages and identifying HV and substation-specific contract, utility, testing, and special inspection requirements.
* Provide technical direction to the HV & Substation Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors assigned to projects, in coordination with the Site Quality Manager, who retains administrative supervision and day-to-day site direction.
* Participate in recruitment, technical interviewing, onboarding, and qualification of discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, and provide performance input to the Site Quality Manager and Regional Quality Manager.
* Develop and deliver discipline-specific training for Quality personnel, covering acceptance criteria, inspection methods, documentation requirements, and common HV and substation failure modes.
* Conduct scheduled jobsite visits to verify implementation of the HV and substation Quality program, perform surveillance of field inspection activities, and audit discipline records in Procore for accuracy, completeness, traceability, and objective evidence.
* Provide technical review and approval of subcontractor Quality Control Plans, ITPs, and inspection forms for HV, substation, and gen-tie scopes prior to acceptance by the Site Quality Manager, and verify subcontractor Quality performance through surveillance and audit.
* Provide technical review and concurrence on proposed repair and use-as-is dispositions for nonconformances within the discipline, and on other dispositions as requested by the Site Quality Manager, in coordination with Engineering.
* Lead or support root cause analysis for significant or recurring HV and substation nonconformances, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure across the portfolio.
* Exercise stop-work authority for quality-driven conditions in accordance with company policy, coordinating through the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact on site.
* Elevate unresolved technical disagreements with site Quality, Construction, or subcontractor personnel to the Regional Quality Manager and Senior Director of Quality, with a documented position and recommended resolution.
* Define Quality’s verification requirements for receiving, storage, preservation, handling, and installation of major HV equipment, including power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, and control enclosures, in alignment with manufacturer requirements.
* Review acceptance test records and third-party test reports for completeness and conformance with ANSI/NETA ATS, project specifications, and manufacturer requirements, and coordinate Quality witness points with testing agencies and Commissioning.
* Define and support Quality’s responsibilities within the functional testing and cold commissioning RACI and in energization-readiness and turnover verification for HV and substation systems, while maintaining clear separation from relay settings, protection coordination, and functional commissioning responsibilities.
* Where required by contract and as directed by the Senior Director of Quality, support factory acceptance test (FAT) witnessing and source inspection of major HV equipment, and contribute to the development of a formal source inspection program as the organization establishes one.
* Coordinate with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, and third-party agencies on HV and substation Quality matters, including utility inspection and witness requirements for facilities built to utility standards.
* Align closely with the Engineering and T&D teams to resolve technical questions, participate in design and constructability reviews, and maintain consistent acceptance criteria across projects.
* Monitor HV and substation Quality KPIs and nonconformance trends across the portfolio, and report findings, emerging risks, and recommendations to the Senior Director of Quality.
* Provide input on discipline staffing and resource planning, including the number and qualification of Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors and third-party testing needs, for estimating and project staffing plans.
* Define the HV and substation Quality records required for turnover and verify completeness of discipline turnover documentation.
* Capture lessons learned from executed projects and incorporate them into discipline templates, training, and the broader Quality Management System (QMS).
* Interact and collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, T&D, Construction, Commissioning, Subcontract Management, and Safety teams to embed Quality into project execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned.
* Travel is required up to 50%, including scheduled jobsite visits, extended site visits, short-notice trips, and overnight stays.

**Key Competencies / Core Skills**

* Recognized technical authority who guides others through credibility and clear reasoning rather than positional authority.
* Translates engineering, manufacturer, utility, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria.
* Builds standardized tools, including ITPs, checklists, SWIs, and Procore templates, that scale across projects, regions, and delivery models.
* Leads effectively within a matrixed structure, supporting the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact while holding the technical standard for the discipline.
* Holds the standard under schedule and commercial pressure while maintaining professional, collaborative working relationships.
* Understands the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, electrical testing, protection and control, and Commissioning, and escalates appropriately.
* Maintains exceptional attention to detail across inspection records, test reports, and supporting objective evidence.
* Analyzes deficiency trends across the portfolio and translates findings into durable process change.
* Communicates clearly and factually with field personnel, engineers, utilities, owners, and executive leadership, both in writing and in person.
* Coaches and develops discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, treating development of the bench as a core responsibility.
* Manages multiple concurrent projects, travel demands, and shifting priorities while maintaining accountability.
* Maintains composure and a solutions-focused approach under pressure, disagreement, and challenging field conditions.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive quality experience in utility-scale renewable-energy, utility, substation, transmission, or industrial electrical construction, including at least 5 years of direct Quality responsibility on high-voltage substation or transmission projects; utility-scale PV electrical experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
* At least 5 years in a quality leadership or management role, including directing inspection personnel or leading Quality programs across multiple projects.
* Demonstrated experience authoring and maintaining ITPs, Quality Inspection Checklists, Standard Work Instructions, and procedures for HV and substation construction.
* Strong working knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, station service equipment, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors.
* Demonstrated ability to read and apply IFC drawings, one-line and three-line diagrams, grounding plans, physical arrangement drawings, schematics and wiring diagrams, cable schedules, specifications, approved submittals, and manufacturer instructions.
* Experience reviewing electrical acceptance test documentation and third-party test reports against ANSI/NETA ATS and project specifications.
* Experience overseeing Quality on both self-performed and subcontracted HV and substation work, including review of subcontractor Quality Control Plans and ITPs.
* Experience coordinating Quality activities with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, testing agencies, and equipment manufacturers.
* Demonstrated experience with nonconformance management, root cause analysis methodology (5-Why, fishbone, fault tree, or equivalent), and corrective action programs.
* Demonstrated understanding of the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, protection and control, and Commissioning responsibilities.
* Proficiency with Procore (Quality & Field Management modules) and SharePoint.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
* Ability to work remotely with a reliable high-speed internet connection and flexibility to support projects across Eastern through Pacific Time Zones as required.
* Must hold and maintain a valid U.S. driver’s license and have the ability to safely operate a motor vehicle, including the ability to rent vehicles for business travel without restrictions that would interfere with job performance.
* Ability to successfully pass a motor vehicle/driving record background check in accordance with company policy.
* Must be able to pass pre-employment, regular, and random drug and alcohol screenings in compliance with company and customer requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional certifications such as:

+ American Society for Quality (ASQ): Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Construction Quality Manager (CCQM), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA)
+ InterNational Electrical Testing Association (NETA): NETA Certified Technician, Level III or Level IV
+ American Welding Society (AWS): Certified Welding Inspector (CWI)
+ American Concrete Institute (ACI): Concrete Field Testing Technician, Grade I
+ Electrical licensing: State journeyman or master electrician license
+ Project Management Institute (PMI): Project Management Professional (PMP)

* Experience witnessing factory acceptance testing or performing source inspection of power transformers, circuit breakers, switchgear, or control enclosures.
* Experience across multiple substation configurations, voltage classes, and equipment manufacturers, including facilities built to interconnecting utility standards and transferred to utility ownership.
* Experience with gen-tie transmission line construction, including foundations, steel structures, conductor and OPGW installation, and associated hardware.
* Working knowledge of NESC (IEEE C2), NEC (NFPA 70), ANSI/NETA ATS, IEEE 80, and IEEE C57 series standards for power transformers.
* Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and formal Quality Management System requirements.
* Experience developing and delivering technical training for Quality or field personnel.
* Advanced proficiency with Procore, including inspection template configuration, reporting, and workflow design, as well as Power BI.
* Experience supporting utility-scale solar PV and BESS projects with integrated substation and interconnection scopes.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish, with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse project teams.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
 
 

* Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while operating a computer and reviewing documentation, drawings, and test records.
* Ability to effectively exchange accurate information in verbal and written form with employees, contractors, utilities, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to conduct regular jobsite visits requiring extended standing and walking on uneven or unpaved terrain, as well as bending, stooping, kneeling, and climbing stairs or ladders to access substation and HV construction areas.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds of inspection equipment, documentation, or other work-related materials as required.
* Ability to perform field activities while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, and arc-rated clothing or other project-specific PPE where required.
* Ability to safely access substation and HV construction areas in accordance with site safety requirements, electrical safe-work practices, qualification requirements, and access controls.
* Ability to travel domestically up to 50% of the time, including by air, with flexibility for short-notice trips, overnight stays, and extended site visits.
* Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
 
 

* Work is divided between a remote/home office environment, requiring reliable high-speed internet and standard office equipment, including audio/video conferencing, and active construction sites.
* Field work is performed at utility-scale substation, high-voltage, gen-tie, solar, and BESS construction sites, where conditions may include outdoor weather exposure, dust, moderate to high noise levels, moving construction equipment, and uneven terrain. Appropriate PPE will be provided and required.
* Field work regularly occurs in proximity to energized or potentially energized facilities as projects progress toward energization, requiring strict adherence to electrical safety requirements, qualification boundaries, and access controls.
* Work schedules during jobsite visits may vary based on construction activities, testing schedules, utility requirements, and project milestones, and may include early starts, extended hours, or weekends.
* Regular interaction with cross-functional teams in both virtual and in-person settings, requiring adaptability to both independent and collaborative work environments.
